label: Daniel P. Sheehan
narrative: Daniel Sheehan is the legal architecture of the disclosure movement. A Harvard College and Harvard Law graduate who worked the Pentagon Papers case, Watergate, Silkwood, Greensboro and the La Penca bombing suit, he founded the Christic Institute and the Romero Institute and now runs the New Paradigm Institute, which lobbies directly for the UAP Disclosure Act. He was counsel to Harvard psychiatrist John Mack and to Steven Greer's Disclosure Project, and he represents Luis Elizondo in litigation against the Department of Defense. His significance for this board is that he is the person converting testimony into legal instruments - eminent domain provisions, records-review boards, whistleblower protection - and the New Paradigm Institute is running the campaign to get the Senate to pass the UAPDA after House action. Sheehan's record also carries a real liability: the Avirgan v. Hull suit was dismissed in 1988 with Rule 11 sanctions of over a million dollars against the Christic Institute, and the presiding judge criticised his reliance on witnesses who were dead, unwilling or one person removed from the facts. That is a hostile-audit vulnerability the board should carry openly, because the same evidentiary pattern - second-hand witnesses, unavailable primaries - recurs in the UAP context.
